articles.title: Champions League 2026-27 draw: Four pots set as 36 clubs discover their league-phase opponents in star-studded fixtures
articles.summary: Football News: The Champions League 2026-27 draw features thrilling matchups including Arsenal vs Real Madrid and Manchester United vs Bayern Munich. Discover the full list of fixtures and the teams involved in this star-studded league phase.
articles.body: The Champions League has its 36-team field, its four seeding pots and, following Thursday's draw in Monaco, a complete set of league-phase opponents. This season's draw has produced several heavyweight meetings, including Arsenal hosting Real Madrid and travelling to Bayern Munich, Liverpool welcoming Atlético Madrid before heading to Inter Milan, and Manchester City being paired with defending champions Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.Manchester United's return to Europe's elite also brings a blockbuster reunion with Bayern Munich at Old Trafford, while Aston Villa have been handed a particularly glamorous reward for winning the Europa League. With every team facing eight different opponents, here is how the new Champions League campaign has been put together.How the Champions League league phase worksThe 36 clubs are divided into four pots according to their UEFA coefficient rankings and results in European competition over the previous five years.Each club is then drawn against two teams from each pot, giving every side eight league-phase matches in total.The schedule is split evenly between home and away fixtures, so every club will play four matches at home and four away. Across the entire league phase, that produces 144 matches.The format also determines what happens after those eight games. The top eight teams in the standings advance directly to the round of 16, while teams finishing from ninth through 24th enter the knockout-phase play-offs. The remaining sides are eliminated.There are also important restrictions on the draw. The five Premier League clubs cannot be drawn against one another during the league phase, while UEFA has introduced a further condition preventing the same fixture from being repeated with the same home team for three consecutive seasons.That means Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid again, while Inter Milan cannot host Arsenal again, after those fixtures were played with the same home teams in the previous two seasons.Pot 1: The European heavyweightsThe first pot contains the defending champions and some of the biggest names in European football, giving the teams drawn from the lower pots the possibility of facing some formidable opposition.Paris Saint-GermainBayern MunichReal MadridLiverpoolInter MilanManchester CityArsenalBarcelonaAtlético MadridParis Saint-Germain enter as the two-time defending European champions, having beaten Arsenal in last season's final.Pot 2: United return alongside European heavyweightsManchester United are back in the Champions League after a two-year absence and will be drawn from the second pot.Borussia DortmundRomaSporting CPAston VillaPortoManchester UnitedClub BruggeReal BetisPSV EindhovenAston Villa also enter this group after winning the Europa League, while Dortmund and Porto bring their own European pedigree.Pot 3: A dangerous middle groundPot 3 contains several clubs capable of making life difficult for the competition's traditional giants.FeyenoordLilleBodø/GlimtNapoliRB LeipzigVillarrealFenerbahçeShakhtar DonetskGalatasarayBodø/Glimt will be particularly familiar to viewers who followed last season's competition. The Norwegian club became one of the stories of the tournament after beating Manchester City, Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan during a remarkable run before reaching the round of 16.Fenerbahçe also return to the competition proper after beating Lyon 3-2 on aggregate in qualifying, their first appearance in the main tournament since 2008-09.Pot 4: The newcomers and potential surprisesPot 4 completes the field, with several clubs making their debut in the competition proper.Slavia PragueSlovan BratislavaStuttgartAEK AthensLASKComoLensVikingSabahViking reached the league phase after beating Dinamo Zagreb 5-3 on aggregate, while Sabah, LASK and Como are also entering the competition proper for the first time. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly 'crying intensely' after Al-Nassr comeback as journalist reveals why he came off at half-time
articles.summary: Football News: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly cried after Al-Nassr's thrilling 3-2 win over Al-Ettifaq, claiming he wasn't fit to continue. Despite being substituted at half-time, Ronaldo passionately cheered on his teammates from the sidelines.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly endured an emotional night despite Al-Nassr completing one of the most remarkable comebacks of their season, with Saudi Arabian media personality Khalid Al-Shanif claiming the Portugal star was "crying intensely" after the 3-2 victory over Al-Ettifaq.The 41-year-old made his first start of the season on Tuesday, but was replaced by Abdullah Al-Khaibari at half-time after Al-Nassr had fallen 2-0 behind and been reduced to 10 men. Al-Shanif has since offered his account of what happened behind the scenes, while manager Ange Postecoglou gave a somewhat different explanation of the substitution, saying Ronaldo was always scheduled to play only the opening 45 minutes.What happened with Ronaldo at half-time?Al-Nassr's night had started badly when goalkeeper Bento was sent off in the 12th minute after bringing down Moussa Dembélé, forcing the team to play almost the entire match with 10 men.Al-Ettifaq then took advantage of the numerical advantage, with Ondrej Duda putting the hosts ahead in the 31st minute before Álvaro Medrán doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.Ronaldo, who had only recently returned to competitive action after an extended break following the 2026 World Cup and his marriage to Georgina Rodríguez, was subsequently replaced at the interval, with Al-Khaibari coming on as Al-Nassr looked to strengthen the team after going down to 10 men.According to Saudi Arabian sports journalist and television presenter Al-Shanif, who discussed the situation on his programme Doreena Ghair, the decision was actually initiated by Ronaldo himself."Cristiano Ronaldo was the one who requested to be substituted against Al-Ettifaq because he wasn't ready and wanted a ready player in his place. Cristiano Ronaldo was crying intensely after Al-Nassr's victory against Al-Ettifaq."Reports and footage from the match also fuelled speculation that Ronaldo was angry with the decision. The Al-Nassr captain was visibly irritated as he removed the armband from his arm and walked off the pitch.Postecoglou says Ronaldo was always meant to play 45 minutesSpeaking after the match, Postecoglou explained that Ronaldo's limited involvement was linked to his fitness rather than a reaction to his performance."Look, again, with Cristiano, he is a unique sportsman. He has not had much preparation, and the plan was always for him to play 45 minutes against Al Ettifaq. He played 30 minutes in the first game, so we wanted him to play 45 against Al Ettifaq and build up gradually."The manager added that Ronaldo had wanted to remain on the pitch after Al-Nassr fell two goals behind."That was always going to happen at half time, but because of the situation, with the team losing 2-0, Cristiano wanted to help and wanted to keep playing. For me, though, those 45 minutes were good because now we know that he is ready to play more than 45 minutes. I know he feels physically in good condition now, so he is ready for tomorrow's game."Ronaldo cheers Al-Nassr's comeback from the sidelinesWhatever the circumstances surrounding the substitution, Ronaldo watched from the sidelines as his team produced a stunning turnaround — and footage from the second half showed him loudly and proudly cheering his teammates on.Al-Nassr came out for the second half two goals down and a man short, but they gradually turned the game around. Sadio Mané pulled one back in the 74th minute after João Félix threaded a pass through to him, giving the visitors a route back into the match.Only three minutes later, Félix provided the delivery again, this time from a corner, and Abdulelah Al-Amri headed Al-Nassr level.With the match seemingly heading towards a draw, Al-Nassr found one final opening in the 90th minute. Sami Al-Najei drove the counter-attack forward before finding Mané, who finished from inside the box to complete his brace and send Al-Nassr from 2-0 down to a 3-2 victory.The celebrations continued inside the dressing room, where visuals showed Ronaldo embracing his teammates after the dramatic turnaround. Despite being unable to influence the result on the pitch, he appeared fully invested in the victory, sharing the emotional scenes with the squad after the final whistle.The result leaves Al-Nassr with a perfect nine points from their opening three Saudi Pro League matches.Ronaldo's return is still being managedRonaldo missed Al-Nassr's opening two league matches against Al-Fateh and Al-Diriyah while taking an extended break following Portugal's World Cup campaign and his wedding to Rodríguez.He returned as a substitute against Al-Riyadh and scored before making his first start of the season against Al-Ettifaq.Postecoglou's comments suggest Al-Nassr are still carefully managing his workload, although the manager believes Ronaldo is now ready to play beyond the 45-minute mark.Al-Nassr will next face Al-Taawoun as they look to maintain their perfect start to the Saudi Pro League season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chelsea agree to sign Lionel Messi's World Cup winning Argentina teammate in £7.5m deal
articles.summary: Football News: Chelsea have agreed a £7.5 million deal to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ahead of the summer transfer deadline, BBC reported.The 33-ye.
articles.body: Chelsea have agreed a £7.5 million deal to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ahead of the summer transfer deadline, BBC reported.The 33-year-old Argentina international is set to undergo a medical in London before joining Chelsea's goalkeeping group at Stamford Bridge.The move comes after concerns over the performances of Robert Sanchez, especially during Chelsea's 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday.Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso had identified signing a goalkeeper as a priority after Sanchez's display against Fulham. The deal for Martinez was completed quickly after that decision.Martinez has fallen out of favour at Aston Villa following the club's signing of Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma earlier this month for around £30 million. Martinez is expected to sign a two-year contract with Chelsea, with an option to extend it by another year.Sanchez has been Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper since 2023. Against Fulham, he allowed Josh King's shot to slip through his hands at the near post. Later in the match, he spilled another effort into a dangerous area, allowing Gonzalo Garcia to score.Chelsea had previously backed Sanchez as their first-choice goalkeeper, but the club has now decided to bring in Martinez just days before the transfer window closes.Chelsea also have Mike Penders, who joined from Genk for £17 million, as another goalkeeping option. He is expected to make his debut in the Carabao Cup against Luton Town on Thursday night.Chelsea are also expected to have a busy end to the transfer window as Manchester City continue their attempts to sign Enzo Fernandez. The Argentina midfielder wants to leave Chelsea and was left out of the squad for Thursday night's Carabao Cup match against Luton.The transfer is another deal between Chelsea and Aston Villa in recent weeks.Chelsea signed Morgan Rogers from Villa for a club-record £117 million, while Alejandro Garnacho moved to Villa on an initial loan deal last month.Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson was completing a medical at Villa Park on Thursday as he prepares to reunite with his former Villarreal manager Unai Emery. Villa value the deal at around £65 million.The two clubs have completed several transfers recently, including Ian Maatsen joining Villa and Omari Kellyman moving to Chelsea in a deal that was widely described as a PSR swap.Martinez had also attracted interest from Juventus earlier in the transfer window, but that move collapsed because of concerns over a finger injury. Juventus later signed Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario on loan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga Preview: Hertha hope to maintain perfect record, Osnabrück seek maiden point
articles.summary: The third matchday of 2. Bundesliga will commence with a couple of fixtures on Friday. Hertha BSC will face Eintracht Braunschweig away from home as they hop...
articles.body:
The third matchday of 2. Bundesliga will commence with a couple of fixtures on Friday. Hertha BSC will face Eintracht Braunschweig away from home as they hope to extend their winning streak, while VfL Bochum host pointless VfL Osnabrück.

Hertha BSC are unbeaten in their last six head-to-head fixtures against Eintracht Braunschweig. Furthermore, the visitors won their first three games of the season, although they needed a penalty shootout to knock out Pokal specialists Saarbrücken.

Eintracht Braunschweig had a dream start to the season with a 6-1 victory over Magdeburg in the opening 2. Bundesliga matchday before home defeats to Bochum and Union Berlin in two competitions.

Deyovaisio Zeefuik is suspended after his red card in Hertha's 4-1 win over Heidenheim, but new signing Mads Pedersen could fill the position. Meanwhile, Marten Winkler, who was involved in three of the goals back then, has since left the club to join Anderlecht.

Braunschweig: Hoffmann; Aydin, Ehlers, Hoti, Katterbach; Flick; Di Benedetto, Marie; Sturm, Entrup, Opoku

Hertha: Gersbeck; Eitschberger, Gechter, Kolbe, Pedersen; Seguin, Sessa; Thorsteinsson, Gouram, Brekalo ©; Grönning

Days before facing FC Bayern in the DFB-Pokal first round tie, Osnabrück will face Bochum away from home in 2. Bundesliga. The newly-promoted side started their campaign with two defeats, although the positives outweigh the 4-3 defeat to Heidenheim on the opening matchday.

Bochum recovered from a home defeat to Hertha in the season's curtain-raiser with victories on the road in 2. Bundesliga and Pokal. Uwe Rösler's men will now have another chance to keep the momentum as they hope to get involved in the promotion race.

Bochum are unbeaten against Osnabrück in eight meetings, with their last head-to-head fixture dating back to the 2020/21 season. However, the Purple-Whites held Bochum to draws in their last two visits to Vonovia Ruhrstadion.

Bochum: Horn ©; Olsen, Steinwender, Mets, Wittek; Cokaj, Pannewig; Miyoshi, Taz, Rasmussen; Hofmann

Osnabrück: Krumrey; Fabinski, Müller ©, Wiemann; Kammerbauer, Wagner, Jacobsen, Abu Hanna; Kyereh, Badjie; Meißner

articles.title: Rodri’s debut, Cubarsi’s return | Three takeaways from Barcelona 2-0 Athletic Club
articles.summary: Barcelona made it six points in two games with their win over Athletic Club last night as they took the Basque giants down with a 2-0 scoreline at the Spotif...
articles.body:
Barcelona made it six points in two games with their win over Athletic Club last night as they took the Basque giants down with a 2-0 scoreline at the Spotify Camp Nou.

Pedri, Pau Cubarsi and Anthony Gordon entered the starting lineup on the night and the team looked comfortable, yet threatening from the get-go.

Raphinha eventually scored the opener with some wonderful footwork and Barcelona toiled to earn the second goal to pull free of the competition.

Eventually, a bit of luck and Fermin Lopez's lethality helped the team secure the 2-0 win and helped them back to the top of the table.

Barça Universal brings you three takeaways from Barcelona 2-0 Athletic Club.

Going purely by the scoreline, Barcelona's win over Elche appears significantly more dominant than their win last night over Athletic Club de Bilbao. The reality, however, is very different.

Unai Simon played a fantastic game against Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Taking to the field last night for the second official game of the season, Barcelona were dominant from the get-go and relentlessly attacked the visitors, even more than they did against Elche.

The scoreline, however, tells a different story, and that was only down to one man – Unai Simon.

On the night at Spotify Camp Nou, the Spanish national team goalkeeper showed his class and bailed his team out of difficult situations repeatedly. In 90 minutes, he made a staggering eight saves, six of which came from inside the box.

Had it not been for Simon, the scoreline could well have been 6-0 or even 7-0 in Barcelona's favour, for they hit the woodwork twice and were denied by Simon's brilliance time and time again beyond the two goals that counted.

If anything, the performance only solidifies the argument that Barcelona's attack looks lethal without a striker for the second straight game. After all, the team created four big chances and had an xG of 4.23 compared to the opposition's 0.25.

Pau Cubarsi made his first official appearance of the new season last night. It was, in fact, his first start in a competitive game since the FIFA World Cup final.

Pau Cubarsi returned to the starting XI. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Rightfully named the Best Young Player at the World Cup, Cubarsi picked up exactly where he left off and showed no signs of rustiness despite playing after over a month.

The young defender's reading of the game was immaculate, and he placed himself in the best strategic position to nullify the opposition's attacking threat. His defensive contributions were well-timed, and his distribution was silky as always.

In 90 minutes, the teenage sensation made two tackles, three clearances and won five duels. He completed 95% of his passes and was crucial to the clean sheet being maintained.

Barcelona's defence looked superior in terms of the cohesion and implementation of the high line with the youngster back, and it is clear at this point that he is another young anomaly of the sport.

His return to club football in top condition, needless to say, comes as a massive boost to Hansi Flick's plans.

The one moment Barcelona's game last night will be remembered for in the years to come was the 63rd minute of the game when the club's latest and marquee signing Rodri took to the field to make his official debut.

Rodri made his official debut for Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Having only completed his transfer last week, it was unclear when fans would get to see him in action for the first time. After all, he also underwent recent surgery on his back.

Despite everything, however, the player began training with the group in no time and came off the bench for his official debut against Athletic Club. He played the final half an hour, and his integration seemed effortless.

Playing in a system constructed to maximise his strengths, Rodri looked comfortable playing as Barcelona's pivot and linked up well with Pedri, Dani Olmo, Cubarsi and Fermin Lopez.

The team instantly shifted to a traditional 4-3-3 after his arrival, making it clear what role Flick sees best suited for Rodri. Pedri moved into an attacking midfield role, and the new signing held the fortress with ease.

There is no doubt that the player is still rusty and will take some time to adapt and enhance his link-up with the existing players. What last night's game showed, however, is that it will not take too long.

In just 27 minutes, the former Manchester City star made 23 accurate passes with an accuracy rate of 88%. He also made one key pass and had three defensive contributions with three ground duels won at a 100% success rate.

It remains to be seen when the player is fit enough to start, but it is safe to say that Rodri's debut was promising and that the team will move several notches up in terms of stability with him holding the fortress.

articles.title: Yan Diomande: A record fee, huge expectations and an early battle for minutes at Real Madrid
articles.summary: Yan Diomande arrived at Real Madrid this summer with a record-breaking price tag and the expectations that come with it. Two games into the 2026/27 La Liga s...
articles.body:
Yan Diomande arrived at Real Madrid this summer with a record-breaking price tag and the expectations that come with it.

Two games into the 2026/27 La Liga season, though, the €125 million signing is still waiting for his first real moment in the spotlight.

Real Madrid have started strongly, and the usual names have taken over the headlines.

As such, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Jr. and Jude Bellingham have driven the early conversation around the club, while Mourinho's new-look side has shown enough attacking fluency to give the manager little reason to force changes.

That has left Diomande in an unfamiliar position, with Real Madrid's most expensive signing playing just over 30 minutes across the opening two league matches.

For a 19-year-old signed from Leipzig, the lack of immediate prominence should not necessarily be mistaken for a lack of belief.

But given the price tag attached to his name, questions are being raised.

Guler's emergence has complicated the picture

Arda Guler is Diomande's immediate competition. (Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images)

Diomande's biggest obstacle is not just the competition created by Vinicius or the presence of Mbappe and Bellingham.

Arda Guler's new role under Jose Mourinho has also changed the balance of Real Madrid's attack.

Mourinho has used a 4-2-3-1 in the first two competitive matches, with Guler beginning from the right before moving into central areas when Madrid have the ball.

The tactical adjustment has given the Turkish international a more prominent role and, in turn, reduced the immediate need for another natural winger.

Diomande was introduced against Espanyol when the score stood at 1-1, offering Mourinho an attacking option during a competitive second half.

His appearance against Real Sociedad was shorter still. With Madrid already in control, the Ivorian replaced Vinicius in the 84th minute.

Those cameos have offered only glimpses of what the Real Madrid hierarchy paid so heavily to acquire.

A record transfer fee does not buy a place

Yan Diomande is Real Madrid's club-record signing. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The Yan Diomande transfer was one of the defining moves of Real Madrid's summer.

At €125 million, with the potential of rising to €140 million, the club made a statement about how highly they rate the teenager.

Yet Mourinho has shown no sign of selecting players according to their transfer fee.

With Real Madrid winning and their attacking structure functioning, the Portuguese coach has understandably placed trust in the players who have started the season well.

Vinicius remains a decisive presence, while Guler's ability to operate from the right and drift into midfield has given Mourinho another tactical solution.

That is the reality Diomande must understand. He is not arriving at a struggling side crying out for reinvention.

Rather, he is trying to break into one of the deepest and most talented attacks in European football.

Indeed, the coming weeks should offer more opportunities, as the fixture list will become heavier and rotation will be required, but that still does not guarantee anything.

Diomande has not played much for Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

There is a temptation to judge a €125 million signing, particularly when the player has been limited to a handful of minutes.

But Diomande's first weeks at Real Madrid may say more about the competition around him than his standing within the club.

At 19, he has time on his side. What he needs now is the right opportunity.

Mourinho's selection against Espanyol and Real Sociedad suggests that Diomande is still being introduced gradually, rather than being handed responsibility because of the size of his transfer.

That approach could frustrate fans expecting an immediate impact, but it also shows the reality of Real Madrid's current attacking strength.

The first opening may come through rotation. When it does, the focus will shift from the size of the Yan Diomande transfer fee to a more important question: can Real Madrid's record signing make himself impossible to leave out?
